prompt: Implement one step of gradient descent for the one-parameter model y = w*x with mean-squared-error loss; results are compared after rounding to 6 decimal places. Complete the step method in the starter file.
explanation: Gradient descent improves a model parameter by nudging it against the slope of the loss: here the loss mean((w*x - y)^2) has derivative mean(2*x*(w*x - y)) with respect to w. Averaging that expression over all data points gives the gradient, and subtracting lr * gradient moves w toward lower error. When w already fits the data perfectly the gradient is zero and the step leaves w unchanged -- exactly what the optimum test verifies.
hints: For each point compute the residual (w * xs[i] - ys[i]), multiply by 2 * xs[i], and add it to a sum.
Divide the sum by xs.length to get the mean gradient.
The updated weight is w - lr * gradient; return it directly.
